bib.title: Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN

question: What causes StyleGAN's characteristic image artifacts, and which changes to generator normalization, progressive growing and regularization remove them and improve quality?
hypothesis: The droplet artifacts come from the generator sneaking signal-strength information past instance normalization; a low perceptual path length (smooth latent-to-image mapping) correlates with image quality; and a capacity problem limits use of the highest resolution.
contributions: Weight demodulation replaces AdaIN/instance normalization and removes droplet artifacts
Lazy regularization: regularizers evaluated every 16 minibatches (R1) without harm
Path length regularizer for a smoother generator, which also makes the generator easier to invert
Progressive growing replaced by skip generator and residual discriminator; resolution-usage analysis motivates larger networks
Projection to W with noise-map regularization enables attribution of generated images to a network

method.summary: Starting from the official TensorFlow StyleGAN (config A), the authors apply a cumulative series of changes (B-F): weight demodulation, lazy regularization, path length regularization, no progressive growing with skip G / residual D, and doubled feature maps at 64^2-1024^2. They report FID, PPL, precision and recall on FFHQ and four LSUN categories, plus a latent projection / attribution test.

training.objective: non-saturating logistic loss with R1 regularization (gamma=10; gamma=100 for config E, LSUN Church and Horse), path length regularizer in configs D-F, style mixing regularization
training.lr: progressive growing configs A-D: start 1e-3 at 8^2, increased gradually by 3x; configs E-F fixed 2e-3

training.warmup: inferred: none beyond progressive-growing fade-in (600k images per resolution) in A-D
training.regularisation: R1 (every 16 minibatches for D), path length (every 8 for G), style mixing, EMA of generator weights, minibatch std layer, equalized learning rate
training.hardware: NVIDIA DGX-1, 8x Tesla V100, TensorFlow 1.14.0, cuDNN 7.4.2

training.seeds: each metric computed 10 times with different random seeds and averaged (evaluation)

metrics.definition: perceptual path length: expected LPIPS distance under small latent perturbations in W, endpoints in W, whole image (no central crop)

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.definition: fraction of generated images similar to training data (Kynkaanniemi et al. 2019)

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: fraction of training data that can be generated

metrics.name: LPIPS projection distance

eval.protocol: Snapshot with lowest FID chosen per run; each metric averaged over 10 random seeds; no significance test.

limits: Image-quality metrics FID and P&R are acknowledged to be texture-biased and blind to some quality differences (Figs 13-14); PPL is used as a complementary signal.
Path length regularization trades FID against PPL on less structured datasets (Table 1 row D, LSUN Car FID 2.83 -> 3.43).
Authors say further increases in network size could give additional benefit, and R1 gamma was not fully tuned.
Training requires tens of thousands of images; reducing data requirements is flagged as future work.
Uncurated figures use truncation psi=0.5; training length and gamma tuned per dataset by hand; no hyperparameter search tooling.
Attribution claim rests on a projection method with specific hyperparameters; they note classifier-based detection may not stay reliable.
